title: Saving and restoring state when the system takes the process away

videos.script:
Lesson 4 ended with a rule. Save on the way to the background, because the kill sends no warning. {{rule}} This lesson is about what to save, and how to put it back.

Not everything on a screen is the same kind of thing. {{kinds}} The sessions in the plan are data, and they belong in a database for good. Which course was open, how far the list was scrolled, and the half-typed session are something else. They only have to last until the user comes back.

You will see where each platform keeps that second kind. {{platforms}} Then you run it. A small program saves the planner's screen, and then kills its own process, hard, with no goodbye. {{kill}} A second run starts from nothing, reads the saved state, and draws the same screen. {{restore}}

Last, you weigh what you saved. {{weigh}} Saving ids is eighty bytes. Saving the whole plan is about two thousand times as much, and that is the difference between a state the system keeps and one it refuses.
